extracted.intended_audience: NIH grant applicants, peer reviewers, and NIH staff involved in review of Research Project Grant (RPG) applications
extracted.subtask_description: Guidance and evaluation framework for peer review of NIH Research Project Grant (RPG) applications (effective for due dates on or after Jan 25, 2025), specifying the factors, scoring, and additional review criteria reviewers must use to assess scientific and technical merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Overall Impact
rubrics_metrics.description: Reviewers will provide an overall impact score to reflect their assessment of the likelihood for the project to exert a sustained, powerful influence on the research field(s) involved, in consideration of the review criteria and additional review criteria (as applicable).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: An application does not need to be strong in all categories to be judged likely to have major scientific impact. Overall impact score should reflect synthesis of Factors 1, 2, and 3 and applicable additional criteria.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor 1: Importance of the Research (Significance & Innovation)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate how important the proposed research is in the context of current scientific challenges and opportunities (Significance) and the extent to which innovation influences that importance (Innovation). Factor 1 receives a 1–9 criterion score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Significance: Assess whether the application addresses an important gap, would solve a critical problem, or create a valuable conceptual/technical advance; evaluate rationale and rigor of scientific background (prior literature/preliminary data). Innovation: Evaluate whether the work applies novel concepts, methods, or technologies or uses existing approaches in novel ways to enhance impact. Note: a project need not be technically novel to be of critical importance.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor 2: Rigor and Feasibility (Approach)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate the scientific quality of the proposed work (approach), including the likelihood that compelling, reproducible findings will result (rigor) and whether the proposed studies can be done and completed in the proposed timeframe (feasibility). Factor 2 receives a 1–9 criterion score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Rigor: Assess potential for unbiased, reproducible, robust data; experimental design and controls; sample size sufficiency and justification; quality of analysis, interpretation, and reporting plans; plans to address relevant biological variables (e.g., sex, age). For human/vertebrate animal research, also assess rigor of interventions/manipulations, justification of outcome variables, generalizability or relevance to subgroups, and appropriateness/diversity of sample. For human subjects/clinical trials, assess adequacy of inclusion plans. Feasibility: Evaluate whether approach is sound and achievable, plans to address emerging challenges, whether uncertainty is balanced by potential advances, recruitment/retention plans for diverse participants, likelihood of achieving enrollment, and for clinical trials whether study timeline and milestones are feasible. Additional items integrated into Factor 2: inclusion criteria/coding (sex/gender, age, race/ethnicity), study timeline (for clinical trials), and plans for valid design and analysis of Phase III clinical trials.

rubrics_metrics.name: Factor 3: Expertise and Resources (Investigator(s) & Environment)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the investigator(s) and institutional resources are appropriate to carry out the proposed work. Factor 3 is evaluated via a dropdown selection rather than a numeric score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Dropdown options: 'Appropriate' (no written explanation needed) or 'Identify need for additional expertise and/or resources' (requires the reviewer to briefly address specific gaps in expertise or resources needed to carry out the project). For investigators: assess background, training, expertise (appropriate for career stage), and for MPI applications, quality of leadership plan. For environment: evaluate whether institutional resources are appropriate to ensure successful execution. The binary choice is intended to focus evaluation on adequacy for proposed work and to reduce undue influence of general reputation.

rubrics_metrics.name: Scoring and Use of Criterion Scores
rubrics_metrics.description: How individual criterion scores relate to the review outcome: Factors 1 and 2 each receive separate 1–9 criterion scores; Factor 3 is a dropdown sufficiency assessment. All three factors are considered when arriving at the overall impact score.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Reviewers should apply the 1–9 scoring scale for Factors 1 and 2 consistently and use the Factor 3 dropdown to flag specific gaps. The overall impact score is a synthesis and can reflect strong potential even if not all factors are strong.

rubrics_metrics.name: Protections for Human Subjects (Additional Review Criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: For research involving non-exempt human subjects, evaluate justification for involvement and proposed protections from research risk according to five review criteria; for exempt research, evaluate exemption justification, human subjects involvement and characteristics, and sources of materials.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Non-exempt criteria: 1) risk to subjects; 2) adequacy of protection against risks; 3) potential benefits to subjects and others; 4) importance of knowledge to be gained; 5) data and safety monitoring for clinical trials. For exempt research: 1) justification for exemption; 2) human subjects involvement and characteristics; 3) sources of materials. Reviewers should refer to the Guidelines for the Review of Human Subjects for additional detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Vertebrate Animals (Additional Review Criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: When live vertebrate animals are involved, evaluate the proposed involvement according to specific criteria addressing procedures, justification, welfare interventions, and euthanasia.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Evaluate: (1) description of proposed procedures including species, strains, ages, sex, and total number; (2) justification for use of animals vs alternatives and appropriateness of species; (3) interventions to minimize discomfort, distress, pain and injury; (4) justification for euthanasia method if not consistent with AVMA Guidelines. See the Worksheet for Review of the Vertebrate Animals Section for more detail.

rubrics_metrics.name: Biohazards (Additional Review Criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: When the proposed research includes biohazards, evaluate whether specific materials or procedures are significantly hazardous to personnel/environment and whether adequate protection is proposed.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess risk level of materials/procedures and sufficiency of proposed protections and containment practices.

rubrics_metrics.name: Resubmissions (Additional Review Criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: As applicable, evaluate the full application as now presented (i.e., assess how previous reviewer concerns were addressed).
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Focus on whether the resubmission adequately addresses prior critiques and whether changes improve scientific and technical merit.

rubrics_metrics.name: Renewals (Additional Review Criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: As applicable, evaluate the progress made in the last funding period for renewal (competing continuation) applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess documented productivity, outcomes relative to aims, and justification for continued support.

rubrics_metrics.name: Revisions (Additional Review Criterion)
rubrics_metrics.description: As applicable, evaluate the appropriateness of the proposed expansion of the scope of the project for revision applications.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess whether the revised scope is scientifically justified and whether the proposed additions are feasible and well-integrated.

rubrics_metrics.name: Authentication of Key Biological and/or Chemical Resources (Additional Review Consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: For projects involving key biological and/or chemical resources, evaluate the brief plans proposed for identifying and ensuring the validity of those resources.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Consider whether proposed authentication procedures are adequate to ensure reproducibility and validity of experimental materials (e.g., cell lines, antibodies).

rubrics_metrics.name: Budget and Period of Support (Additional Review Consideration)
rubrics_metrics.description: Evaluate whether the budget and the requested period of support are fully justified and reasonable in relation to the proposed research.
rubrics_metrics.guidance: Assess realism and appropriateness of requested resources and duration; do not give a separate numeric score but consider in the overall impact determination as applicable.
